identity.real_world_identity_notes: The 1996 short-tail evolution of the McLaren F1 GTR. It retained and strengthened the earlier H-pattern manual gearbox; the six-speed sequential belongs to the separately curated 1997 Longtail.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: The 1996 F1 GTR used a six-speed H-pattern manual. Its construction, exact gate, and real clutch/lift/blip technique are not established by the reviewed sources.
The fingerprinted AC implementation requires the clutch to move off, rejects a full-throttle upshift until the driver lifts, and rejects a coast downshift until the driver blips.
This is not the 1997 Longtail. McLaren states that the six-speed sequential gearbox arrived with that later car.
Observed live in AC 14923034 via guided verification observation ac.mclaren-f1-gtr.20260822t164053064z-b85b3abb by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted AC implementation stalled or refused move-off without physical clutch input.

confidence.basis: Direct guided move-off test with automatic clutch disabled.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted AC implementation accepted the running upshift without physical clutch after the driver lifted.
The fingerprinted AC implementation refused the full-throttle upshift and accepted it after the driver lifted.
The fingerprinted AC implementation refused the full-throttle upshift rather than cutting for the driver.
The fingerprinted AC implementation accepted the running downshift without physical clutch after the driver blipped.
The fingerprinted AC implementation refused the coast downshift and accepted it after the driver's throttle blip.
The fingerprinted AC implementation supplied no automatic throttle blip.

confidence.basis: Direct guided throttle observation during the downshift test.

The official Dream Pack package, exact ks_mclaren_f1_gtr content id, and Kunos's installed 1996-specific description establish the intended implementation. McLaren distinguishes the 1996 evolution from the sequential 1997 Longtail, and evo explicitly identifies the 1995/96 cars as H-pattern manuals. Construction and real-car clutch/lift/blip technique remain unknown rather than being inferred from the simulator.

claims.basis: Kunos's installed metadata describes the 1996 bodywork, magnesium gearbox housing, 1010 kg weight and straight-line comparison with the 1997 Longtail. McLaren says the 1997 car replaced the road-car gearbox with a six-speed sequential, while specialist generational testing identifies 1995/96 as H-pattern. These facts exclude the existing 1997 sequential record.

McLaren establishes that the sequential gearbox arrived for 1997; evo specifies an H-pattern manual for 1995 and 1996. The guided drive selected six H-pattern gears. No reviewed source establishes synchromesh versus dog engagement, the exact H gate, or real driver technique, so those authentic fields stay unknown and the measured AC technique is carried only as simulator overrides.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The generic AC title would collide with the existing 1997 record, but Kunos's own metadata describes the 1996 short-tail specification. Identity is resolved before behavior, so the H-pattern drive creates a separate real-car record rather than being recorded as a contradiction on the Longtail.

The official AC cockpit is the current evidence for the round continuous rim without integrated display or shift lights; no reviewed real-car source independently specifies those wheel-electronics fields.
driver_summary: 1996 six-speed H-pattern car, not the 1997 sequential Longtail. AC requires the clutch to launch, a lift to upshift, and a manual blip to downshift; the real car's detailed technique is not yet sourced.

archetype.basis: The real car is established only as a six-speed H-pattern manual. Gearbox construction, exact gate, and real clutch/lift/blip technique remain unknown, so assigning a technique archetype would turn gaps into claims.
